segments.narration: A catastrophic collapse erased a canyon overnight. In March 1928, California's brand-new St. Francis Dam suddenly gave way, unleashing a deadly flood.
Twelve billion gallons of reservoir surged into the darkness, sweeping away houses, bridges, and entire families without warning.
How does solid concrete just dissolve? Chief engineer William Mulholland had staked his legendary reputation on this massive curved wall.
The terrifying truth wasn't bad cement. The dam's western abutment was built directly onto an ancient, prehistoric landslide that turned to mush when soaked.
When the foundation slaked like dry clay, the monolith sheared in half. It remains the deadliest civil engineering failure in American history.

accuracy_flags.claim: A two-hundred-foot wall of water destroyed the St. Francis Dam in 1928.
accuracy_flags.note: The dam was not destroyed by a wall of water; defective soil foundations and design flaws caused the dam to collapse, which subsequently created the catastrophic flood.

verdicts.claim: A two-hundred-foot wall of water destroyed the St. Francis Dam in 1928.

verdicts.correction: A catastrophic collapse erased a canyon overnight. In March 1928, California's brand-new St. Francis Dam suddenly gave way, unleashing a deadly flood.

verdicts.claim: The massive concrete structure was resting on ancient, unstable landslide debris.
verdicts.note: The reference articles describe the rock formations (conglomerate, sandstone, and mica schist) and a defective soil foundation, but do not mention ancient or prehistoric landslide debris.

verdicts.claim: Chief engineer William Mulholland famously missed the fatal geological fault line.
verdicts.note: The text notes the inactive San Francisquito Fault line and mentions Mulholland acknowledged geological problems, but does not state that he famously missed the fault line.

verdicts.claim: Water infiltration reacted with the soft conglomerate rock, liquefying its foundation.
verdicts.note: The reference mentions percolation tests and a defective soil foundation, but is silent on water infiltration reacting with conglomerate rock or liquefying the foundation.

verdicts.claim: The disaster triggered the end of self-regulated civil engineering projects in California.
verdicts.note: The reference mentions it was one of the worst civil engineering disasters and ended Mulholland's career, but is silent on whether it ended self-regulated civil engineering projects in California.
